query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a moderate cold working treatment (approximately 8% cold rolling reduction) followed by a controlled annealing heat treatment will refine the microstructure and boost both strength and ductility of the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy, thereby enhancing its creep resistance and corrosion performance under extreme conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy produced by conventional casting.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to an 8% cold rolling reduction followed by an optimized annealing treatment to promote partial recrystallization and lamella refinement.
generation.conditions: Intended for fasteners operating under extreme temperature fluctuations (from room temperature up to 700°C), long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep conditions, and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Cold rolling increases dislocation density and refines the lamellar architecture; subsequent annealing facilitates partial recrystallization and further lamella refinement, forming an ultrafine duplex microstructure that enhances work hardening and crack-arresting capability.
generation.mechanism: The cold deformation introduces a high density of dislocations which, coupled with a controlled annealing process, refines the eutectic lamellae. This microstructural refinement enhances dislocation interactions and increases the inherent work-hardening capacity. In turn, these changes improve yield strength and fracture resistance while also benefiting creep behavior and maintaining corrosion resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated alloy is expected to exhibit a significant increase in yield strength and ultimate tensile stress with moderately retained ductility, improved creep resistance, and enhanced corrosion performance relative to the untreated as-cast condition.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA with its initial uniform, fine lamellar microstructure that currently provides insufficient strength and plasticity for industrial fastener applications.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are anticipated when the cold rolling reduction is maintained near 8% and annealing parameters are carefully optimized. Excessive deformation or overly aggressive heat treatment may lead to embrittlement or lamellar coarsening, which must be avoided.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvements in mechanical and corrosion properties are uncertain and will depend on precise processing parameters; further experimental optimization is needed to determine the optimal processing window.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA specimens: one group to be processed with an 8% cold rolling reduction followed by controlled annealing, and a control group left in the as-cast condition. Subject both groups to standardized tests including tensile tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures, room-temperature creep experiments under constant load, and electrochemical corrosion tests simulating corrosive service conditions.
measurements: Tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength
Creep rate under a fixed stress at room temperature
Corrosion current density and potential from electrochemical tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the cold-rolled and annealed specimens do not achieve statistically significant improvements in yield strength, creep resistance, and corrosion performance—without a detrimental loss in ductility—when compared to the as-cast alloy, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, with an fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution and a uniform and fine lamellar microstructure, exhibited the combination of both high fracture strength and high ductility, which has never been achieved in previously reported HEAs. The room temperature tensile test showed a fracture stress of 944 MPa and an elongation of 25.6%, from the engineering stress-strain curve given in Fig. 4a. These values converted to 1186 MPa and 22.8% in the true stress/strain condition. Noteworthily, this alloy exhibited an ultra-high strain hardening behavior, having the proof stress (the proof stress is determined by shifting the linear elastic curve to 0.2% strain. We choose to not to call it the yield stress, as the mechanism for such a low elastic limit is still unclear at this stage.) of 75 MPa but reaching the fracture stress close to 1.2 GPa. At elevated temperatures of 600 and 700°C (Fig. 4b), the proof stress, fracture stress and elongation were 95 MPa, 806 MPa, 33.7%, and 108 MPa, 538 MPa, 22.9%, respectively, both in the true stress/strain condition.
